Duration::lt¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Series Duration::lt(const Duration& other) const;
Series Duration::operator<(const Duration& other) const;  // lt(other)

What It Does¶

Compares two Duration values elementwise, testing whether self is strictly less than other by underlying elapsed-nanosecond magnitude, broadcasting under ordinary N-D rules, and returns a Series of booleans.

Parameters¶

other (const Duration&)

The duration to compare against. Broadcasts against self.

Returns¶

Series A boolean Series at the broadcasted shape, one comparison result per position.

Examples¶

Example 1. 1 hour is less than 90 minutes.

auto ninety_min = pluss::duration::minutes(90);
auto one_hour = pluss::duration::hours(1);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(one_hour.lt(ninety_min));

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=true

1 hour < 90 minutes is true (60 < 90).

Notes¶

  • Comparisons are purely by elapsed magnitude, including sign — a negative Duration compares as less than a positive one, same as ordinary signed-number comparison.

  • operator< is documented sugar for lt — nothing is computed differently between the two spellings.

See Also¶

  • le: the non-strict counterpart.

  • gt, ge: the opposite-direction comparisons.

  • eq, ne: equality comparisons.
